score.moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat, 5/10 — the peer-consistent grade for a diversified specialty insurer (ACGL, AFG, AIZ and RNR all scored 5 in this sweep). Return evidence first, as required: fundamentals.json's roic_proxy series is null for every year and its gross_margin is null, because ORI files no OperatingIncomeLoss tag (annual operating_income is null in fundamentals.json) — for an insurer neither ROIC-on-operating-income nor gross margin is computable from the tags, so the return evidence is the filer's own operating ROE and combined ratio. Those support 5, not 7+: operating return on beginning equity was 14.1% in FY2025 (Q4 2025 earnings call) and 12.1% annualized in H1 2026 (Q2 2026 call), book value per share rose 22.0% in FY2025 inclusive of dividends to $24.21, and the consolidated combined ratio stayed below 100% through the cycle (92.6% FY2023, 93.9% FY2024, 94.7% FY2025) — returns above the cost of capital, earned by underwriting discipline and a diversified specialty + title platform rather than by any structural pricing power: capacity is fungible, brokers can move the business, and the combined ratio has drifted up for three straight years (95.3% in Q2 2026). A moat of 7+ would need durable pricing power or switching costs this record does not show. CAP = 2 + 1.3 x 5 = 8.5 years.

base_override.reason: Insurer payable-earnings base (Andrew, 2026-10-19; WORKER_SPEC step 4): ORI is a P&C/specialty insurer (EDGAR SIC 6351, Surety Insurance — within the rule's 6331/6351 scope) whose releases and annual report print operating income attributable to common shareholders (labelled net income excluding investment gains/losses, i.e. operating income) every period. Consolidated OCF capitalizes the reserve build and unearned-premium float (FY2025 OCF adjustments include +$354.9M of loss-reserve build and +$260.6M of unearned premiums and other policyholder liabilities), so the engine's OCF-based median base of $4.2907/share is not what common shareholders earn — the filer's own operating income was $3.15/share diluted in FY2025. Construction: ($935,900,000 + $845,100,000 + $749,500,000 + $797,000,000 + $792,500,000) = $4,120,000,000; / 5 = $824,000,000; / 251,313,860 diluted shares = $3.2788/share. Five-year average rather than 3-year median because an insurance cycle is longer than three years: the window spans the FY2021 investment-gain year, the FY2022-23 soft underwriting years and the FY2024-25 hard-market years. Figures are as printed in millions to one decimal place, so each carries up to $50K of rounding. With this base in force the one-notch tier_override softening (2026-10-15) is NOT applied — make_score refuses the pair as double-counting; the sector-misfit low confidence and alert suppression stay.
base_override.source: Net income excluding investment gains (losses) — the company's non-GAAP operating income attributable to shareholders — from the GAAP reconciliation table 'Overall Results Attributable to Shareholders' in Old Republic's 2025 Annual Report (the same reconciliation management presents in its earnings releases and 10-K reporting): FY2021 $935.9M, FY2022 $845.1M, FY2023 $749.5M, FY2024 $797.0M, FY2025 $792.5M (all as printed, in millions to one decimal). Cross-checks: the Q4/FY2024 earnings release (PRNewswire, Jan 23, 2025) prints FY2024 $797.0M and FY2023 $749.5M on the identical line; the FY2025 results summary prints FY2025 $792.5M, down 0.6% vs FY2024; the 2026 proxy pay-versus-performance table's Operating Income column prints the same five figures. Denominator: FY2025 diluted shares 251,313,860 (financials_history.csv shares_diluted, latest row).

description.text: (a) General Description of Business. Old Republic International Corporation is a Chicago-based holding company engaged in the business of insurance underwriting and related services. It conducts its business through a number of operating companies, which utilize one or more insurance company subsidiaries to issue their policies, and is organized into two segments: Specialty Insurance and Title Insurance. References herein to such segments apply to the Company's subsidiaries engaged in these respective segments of business. The results of the Republic Financial Indemnity Group (RFIG) Run-off business, previously a reportable segment, are deemed immaterial and reflected within the Corporate & Other caption of this report through the effective date of its sale of May 31, 2024, along with the results of a small life and accident insurance business. "Old Republic" or "the Company" refers to Old Republic International Corporation, its subsidiaries, and any variable interest entities that meet the requirements for consolidation, as the context requires. The insurance business is distinguished from most others in that the prices (premiums) charged for most products are set without knowing what the ultimate loss costs will be. The Company also cannot know exactly when claims will be paid, which may be many years after a policy was issued or expired. This casts Old Republic as a risk-taking enterprise managed for the long run.

about.description_short: Old Republic is a leading specialty insurer that operates diverse property & casualty and title insurance companies. Founded in 1923 and a member of the Fortune 500®, we are a leader in underwriting and risk management services for business partners across the United States and Canada. Our specialized operating companies offer significant expertise in their fields, enabling us to provide tailored solutions that set us apart.

# ORI — Old Republic International Corporation
v5 run, engine release 5.5.0, 2026-10-20. Price $39.68 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $9.972B (key_numbers.md; price × diluted shares) — in scope under $40B. **Finance sector — the OE/capex DCF fits insurers poorly; confidence is low by rule, the model_fit is "misfit", and the tier is a screen result, not an insurer valuation. For this name the engine's OCF base is not the owner's earnings either — see the payable-earnings base below.**

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm/fundamentals outputs, financials_history.csv, or the company's filings and releases as returned by search — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Chicago-based insurance holding company founded in 1923, operating two engines: **Specialty Insurance** (commercial auto, workers' compensation, general liability, property, financial indemnity, surety, home/auto warranty) and **Title Insurance** (one of the largest U.S. title underwriters), plus a small Corporate & Other segment (the RFIG run-off sat there until its sale on May 31, 2024). FY2025 (company results summary): net premiums and fees earned of $8.1B, up 10.1% — Specialty $5.2B, up 10.9%, underwriting income $352.6M at a 93.2% combined ratio; Title $2.9B, up 9.1%, underwriting income $69.9M at a 97.6% combined ratio — consolidated revenue $9,136,300,000 (financials_history.csv), consolidated combined ratio 94.7%, net income $935,400,000, book value per share $24.21, up 22.0% inclusive of dividends declared. Latest quarter, Q2 2026 (earnings call / 10-Q coverage): net income jumped 58% to $324.4M, but nearly all of the increase was investment gains (+$172.4M, including $134.2M unrealized on equities); net operating income **fell** 11% to $186.0M, $0.76 per diluted share vs $0.83, at a 95.3% consolidated combined ratio (Specialty 95.5% with a $40M reserve strengthening; Title 95.1% with pretax operating income more than doubling to $56M). Book value per share $25.33 at Q2 2026, up 7.2% year-to-date including dividends.

## Owner's earnings — the payable-earnings base
**The two engine definitions (FY2025, financials_history.csv, override-filled):** operating cash flow $1,164,300,000; capex $39,300,000 — by override, see OVERRIDE (capex); SBC $46,700,000 (AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025 (engine definition): $1,078,300,000 = $4.29/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total $1.078B, latest FY OE/share $4.29).
- **Maintenance version FY2025: $935,400,000** (financials_history.csv oe_maintenance).
- **Normalized engine base (median of last 3 FY OE/share): $4.29/share** (key_numbers.md) — OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years.

**Why the OCF base is rejected (payable-earnings rule, Andrew 2026-10-19):** ORI is a P&C/specialty insurer — EDGAR SIC **6351 (Surety Insurance)**, inside the rule's 6331/6351 scope (dcf_numbers.json payable_base) — whose filings print operating income attributable to common shareholders every period, labelled "net income excluding investment gains (losses)" (operating income). Consolidated OCF capitalizes policyholder float: the FY2025 cash-flow reconciliation in the annual report adds back a **$354.9M loss and loss adjustment expense reserve build** and a **$260.6M increase in unearned premiums and other policyholder liabilities** — premiums collected and reserves accrued are operating cash flow long before they are earnings available to common shareholders, and the consolidated figure also carries the title segment's escrow-adjacent flows. The result is a $4.29/share base for a company whose own operating income was **$3.15 per diluted share in FY2025**. The one-notch softening (2026-10-15) is not stacked on top of the payable base — make_score refuses the pair as double-counting; tier_override is null.

**Base used = five-year average operating income available to common, $3.28/share, via base_override {basis: payable_earnings_5y, kind: filing} and the `--base-judgment` pin** (key_numbers.md, "Payable-earnings base"):
- Figures (oldest first, exact as printed): **$935,900,000 / $845,100,000 / $749,500,000 / $797,000,000 / $792,500,000** (FY2021–FY2025 net income excluding investment gains/losses, from the GAAP reconciliation table "Overall Results Attributable to Shareholders" in the 2025 Annual Report; cross-checked against the Q4/FY2024 earnings release — FY2024 $797.0M, FY2023 $749.5M on the identical line — and the 2026 proxy pay-versus-performance Operating Income column, which prints the same five figures).
- **Average: $824,000,000 · shares diluted (latest): 251,313,860 · per ordinary share: $3.28** (pinned base $3.2788; key_numbers.md prints the construction — quoted, not retyped from the filing).
- Five-year average, not the 3-year median, because a catastrophe/underwriting cycle is longer than three years: the window spans the FY2021 investment-gain year, the soft FY2022–23 underwriting years and the hard-market FY2024–25 years. The figures are as printed in millions to one decimal, so each carries up to $50K of rounding — immaterial against an $824.0M average.
- OE yield on the scored base: **8.26%** at $39.68 (key_numbers.md diagnostics).

**TTM check (STALE_FY):** ttm.py cannot build a TTM OE for ORI — it exits 3 ("sbc: no post-FY YTD fact": the Allocated SBC tag is filed only in the 10-K, no 10-Q leg exists), so no ttm.json exists and no TTM pin is used; the final pass is pinned with `--base-judgment` in place of `--ttm`, as the payable rule prescribes. The TTM evidence from fundamentals.json (through 2026-06-30) is: revenue **$9,716,900,000** (+12.1% YoY), net income **$1,138,100,000** (investment-gain flattered), operating cash flow **$1,279,900,000**. The operating story inside it is weaker than the headline: Q2 2026 net operating income fell 11% YoY to $186.0M ($0.76/share). That deterioration is carried in the scenario starts below, not in a TTM base.

## OVERRIDE — capex (bounded worker authority, estimate kind, ack'd out-of-band; depreciation anchor stated explicitly)
- **The gap:** the preliminary run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP:capex` — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 and every other year under every candidate tag. EDGAR companyfacts for CIK 74260 contains no PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment fact in any period, and ORI's Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows present no purchases-of-property-and-equipment line in any year — investing activities are maturities/sales/purchases of securities, other investments and short-term investments, with premises/equipment spend folded into "Other investments" / "Other — net" and not isolable from the filing (statements.py confirms: "capex: no capital-expenditure figure is filed for 69 period(s)").
- **The anchor, stated explicitly as the 2026-10-18 clause requires: this capex estimate anchors on filed depreciation because no capex was ever filed for this company.** judgment.json carries `capex_override = {value: 39300000, kind: "estimate"}` — $39,300,000 is **1.0× the filer's filed FY2024 depreciation** (us-gaap Depreciation: FY2023 $33,000,000, FY2024 $39,300,000, FY2025 $35,400,000 in financials_history.csv), i.e. the top of the filed FY2023–FY2025 range, within the 0.1×–10× band around that depreciation anchor, with an `ack_reason` recording that the engine marks it out-of-band by construction because no filed capex value exists to anchor the plain band. Maintenance capex for an insurer (premises, IT, leasehold) is proxied by its own depreciation — the standard maintenance-capex proxy — at the conservative end of the range.
- **Materiality / measured impact (key_numbers.md):** base OE/share $3.28 (no override) → $3.28 (with override), +0.00%; weighted IRR 11.72% → 11.72%. **Unblocks tier: YES** — without it the filing gap blocks scoring entirely. The scored base is the payable operating-income base, which already carries the depreciation charge inside net income, so the proxy does not move the verdict; it unblocks the engine's OCF history.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow; discipline and diversification, no structural pricing power
Return evidence first: fundamentals.json's `roic_proxy` series is null for every year and gross margin is null, because ORI files no OperatingIncomeLoss tag — for an insurer neither is computable from the tags, so the return evidence is the filer's own operating ROE and combined ratio. Operating return on beginning equity was **14.1% in FY2025** and **12.1% annualized in H1 2026**; book value per share rose **22.0% in FY2025** inclusive of dividends; the combined ratio stayed below 100% through the cycle (**92.6% FY2023, 93.9% FY2024, 94.7% FY2025**). That is a real, durable franchise earning above its cost of capital — and it is also the ceiling of the claim: returns come from underwriting discipline and diversification, not pricing power, and the combined ratio has drifted up three straight years. Peers ACGL, AFG, AIZ and RNR all scored 5 in this sweep; ORI's record does not justify more. CAP = 2 + 1.3 × 5 = **8.5 years**; growth holds 2 years, then fades to the 2.5% terminal rate over the CAP.
- **FOR:** diversified two-engine platform — Specialty plus a top-tier U.S. title insurer; title carried Q2 2026 when specialty softened, specialty carried FY2024 · conservative reserving over a century (founded 1923) — favorable prior-year development of 2.4 points in FY2025 and 2.9 points in Q4 2024 · sustained operating returns — operating ROE 14.1% FY2025, combined ratio 92.6–94.7% across FY2023–FY2025 · capital-return engine — $1,708M returned in FY2024, dividends paid TTM $912,100,000 and buybacks TTM $318,500,000 (fundamentals.json), diluted shares down from 303,667,669 (FY2021) to 251,313,860 (FY2025), regular dividend increased for 44+ consecutive years.
- **AGAINST:** insurance capacity is close to a commodity — no network effects, low switching costs, pricing set by a softening cycle · combined ratio drifting the wrong way — 92.6% → 93.9% → 94.7% → 95.3% (Q2 2026), with commercial-auto / long-haul trucking loss trends and a $40M reserve strengthening in Q2 2026 · title is a housing-transaction derivative, hostage to mortgage rates and volumes · operating income is flat in total dollars — $935.9M (FY2021) vs $792.5M (FY2025); all per-share growth has been bought back, not grown, and H1 2026 operating income fell YoY · reserve risk is the balance sheet — the favorable-development tailwind can reverse, and Q2 2026 specialty development was already slightly unfavorable.

## DCF — engine 5.5 final run (2026-10-20)
Payable base $3.28/share, moat 5 (CAP 8.5 yrs), terminal growth 2.5%, probs 15/30/30/15/10, mults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 (defaults — the payable base is already a through-cycle average, so the multipliers express cycle deviation around it; probabilities are tilted one step bearish vs the 10/25/30/25/10 default because H1 2026 operating income fell and the combined ratio is drifting up).

**Growth-start sanity check (mandatory):** the engine's blend is **12.99%** (rev CAGR 5y 4.98% · rev CAGR 3y 4.16% · latest rev YoY 10.99% · OE/share CAGR 2y 22.08%, plus the +5.00% buyback adjustment on revenue components). That blend measures the wrong quantity for the scored base: the 22.08% OE/share CAGR is an OCF trough-to-recovery artifact (FY2023 OCF $880,400,000 → FY2025 $1,164,300,000) amplified by a shrinking share count, while the scored base's own numerator — operating income — printed **$797,000,000 in FY2024 and $792,500,000 in FY2025 (−0.6%)** on +10.1% premium growth, because the combined ratio rose; operating EPS grew just +4.0% to $3.15, and H1 2026 operating income fell year over year. The starts below are therefore recalibrated to operating-earnings evidence, with revenue prints as the ceiling, not the guide: base 5.0% ≈ buyback pace (~4–6%/yr share shrink) plus near-zero total operating growth; bull 9.0% ≈ the FY2023–25 operating-EPS pace in a firm market; super bull 14.0% pairs the 1.25× multiplier with sustained double-digit premium growth (FY2025 revenue +10.99%, TTM revenue +12.1%) plus operating leverage — a 10%-probability tail, not an expectation; bear 0.0% is the H1 2026 trajectory extended; super bear −4.0% is a reserve-charge / title-slump year (FY2022 operating income fell 9.7% in total on a milder version).

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | IV@15 | IV@12 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | -4.0% | 0.75 | $15.37 | $19.85 | 7.08% |
| Bear | 30% | -0.0% | 0.9 | $21.80 | $28.49 | 9.27% |
| Base | 30% | 5.0% | 1.0 | $29.83 | $39.51 | 11.96% |
| Bull | 15% | 9.0% | 1.1 | $38.72 | $51.81 | 14.72% |
| Super bull | 10% | 14.0% | 1.25 | $54.01 | $73.13 | 18.96% |

- **Weighted: IRR 11.72% · IV@15% $29.00 · IV@12% $38.46 · IV@10% $49.00** (key_numbers.md). Upside at 15%: **-26.9%** — the $39.68 price sits above the weighted IV@15%.
- **Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $29.00 · 20% at $20.49 · 25% at $15.80.**
- Diagnostics: OE yield 8.26% · TV share @15% 18.6% · scenario spread 3.52x · months since FY end 9.6.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:capex** (preliminary run): resolved by the depreciation-anchored estimate override — see OVERRIDE (capex). data_gap_uncovered is empty in the final run.
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.6 months ago): resolved by the TTM check in the Owner's earnings section — ttm.py exits 3 on the SBC leg (the Allocated tag is annual-only), fundamentals.json TTM through 2026-06-30 is quoted there, and the base is the five-year payable pin (`--base-judgment` in place of `--ttm` per the insurer rule). The H1 2026 operating decline is in the scenario starts.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking 6.1%/yr, share CAGR -6.07%): real and central — diluted shares fell from 303,667,669 (FY2021) to 251,313,860 (FY2025). The engine credits +5.00% to the revenue components only; my scenario starts are set on operating evidence independently of that credit, and they assume the buyback continues at roughly its recent pace — if capital return shifts further toward special dividends (FY2024: $766M dividends / $942M buybacks; TTM: $912,100,000 dividends / $318,500,000 buybacks, fundamentals.json), per-share growth undershoots the base start. The payable base denominator is the latest filed count, deliberately.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK**: the engine found no debt tag in any year, so its net debt is null — stated from the filing instead: at December 31, 2025 total assets were $29,862,700,000, total liabilities $23,934,200,000 and shareholders' equity $5,914,000,000 (financials_history.csv). The borrowing the engine missed is the senior-notes stack in the debt note (Q3 2025 10-Q, Note 7): 3.875% notes due 2026 $549.0M, 5.750% notes due 2034 $396.2M, 3.850% notes due 2051 $643.4M — **total debt carrying value $1,588.7M at December 31, 2024 and $1,589.6M at September 30, 2025**; the March 31, 2026 capitalization table in the company's 2026 notes-offering prospectus supplement shows total debt $1,590.1M, a 26.9% debt-to-equity ratio. The bulk of the liability side is policyholder float, not financial debt — loss and LAE reserves $14,815.2M and unearned premiums $4,153.4M at September 30, 2025 (Q3 2025 release balance sheet). Holding-company leverage is modest; no HIGH_NET_DEBT verdict is taken from the engine either way.
- **CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED**: the only cash tag filed is the combined cash + restricted-cash total — $263,200,000 at FY2025 (financials_history.csv) — and no filed tag separates the restricted part (statements.json carries the same warning for 24 periods), so any net-debt figure would be understated by that unknown restricted amount. No leverage conclusion in this analysis rests on the cash line; the debt note above is the leverage evidence.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Finance): accepted in full. An insurer's distributable earnings are bounded by statutory capital and reserving, its float-funded OCF is not owner's earnings, and value is normally judged on operating ROE vs cost of equity and price/book — at $39.68 the market pays ~1.6× the FY2025 book value of $24.21 for a 14.1% operating ROE, which is the cross-check the verdict below rests on. Confidence is low, model_fit is "misfit", and score.json suppresses the alert (sector misfit; the tier also rests on judgment overrides).
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex**: see OVERRIDE (capex) — gap, depreciation anchor stated explicitly, ack_reason, and the measured impact (+0.00% on the payable base; unblocks the tier).
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier D at 9.27% vs bull tier C at 14.72%): accepted — the verdict spans tiers because the underwriting cycle does. Any position sizing belongs at the bear end.

## My thoughts / overlay
- **The method range is the honest headline.** On the payable base with the engine's unadjusted blend starts and default probabilities, this same run printed **Tier B, weighted IRR 16.29%** in the intermediate pass — a result built on a 13% growth start for a company whose operating income shrank last year. On the rejected OCF median base ($4.29/share, ~31% above the payable base) it would print higher still, on float. The scored pairing — payable base, operating-evidence starts — prints **Tier C, 11.72%**. Anyone quoting one number for ORI without its base and its growth start is hiding the ball.
- The insurer cross-check agrees with C: $39.68 is ~1.6× FY2025 book value ($24.21) and ~1.57× Q2 2026 book ($25.33) for a franchise printing 12–14% operating ROE with a rising combined ratio and flat total operating income. That prices in roughly low-teens expected returns — exactly the weighted case, with no margin for the bear case (9.27%, IV@15% $21.80).
- The dividend is real but partly special: DPS and the $912,100,000 of TTM dividends paid include special dividends ($2.00/share paid January 2025; a further $2.50/share special was declared in late 2025) — capital return is the bull fuel here, and it is a policy choice that can slow, not a franchise growth rate.
- What would change the verdict: the price falling to the weighted IV@15% of $29.00 (at which point the weighted case itself clears 15%); the combined ratio returning to ~93% with operating EPS compounding at the bull start; or a reserve charge / title collapse that makes the bear case the base case. Q3 2026 results (due late October 2026) are the next evidence on the combined-ratio drift.

## Final verdict
**Tier C — weighted IRR 11.72%, IV@15% $29.00 vs the $39.68 price; sized to the bear end (Tier D, 9.27%).** A disciplined, diversified, century-old insurer with a moderate moat (5/10), scored the only honest way this sweep scores insurers — on what common shareholders actually earn ($3.28/share, five-year average operating income), not on float-inflated OCF ($4.29/share). At $39.68 the market already pays for the base case: the stock clears Andrew's 15% hurdle only at or below **$29.00**, the 20% hurdle at $20.49 and the 25% hurdle at $15.80. Confidence low (sector misfit); no alert (misfit suppression, and the tier rests on judgment overrides).
